'''Irina Grigorieva, Lady Geim''' is a Professor of Physics at the [[University of Manchester]] and Director of the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] Centre for Doctoral Training in Science and the Applications of Graphene. She was awarded the 2019 David Tabor Medal and Prize of the [[Institute of Physics]] and was elected as a Fellow of the Institute.

== Early life and education ==
Grigorieva was born in [[Russia]]. She studied physics at the [[Institute of Solid State Physics (Russia)|Institute of Solid State Physics]] in [[Russia]] and earned her PhD in 1989.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.research.manchester.ac.uk/portal/en/researchers/null(62b1a95b-7b0d-45c0-87a1-e4733fb30e94).html|title=Prof Irina Grigorieva {{!}} The University of Manchester|website=www.research.manchester.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2019-07-02}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/irina-grigorieva-12702/|title=Irina Grigorieva {{!}} Royal Society|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2019-07-02}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
In 1990, Grigorieva moved to [[Nottingham]] with her husband [[Andre Geim]].<ref name="Cover Story - The godfather of graphene | 1843 magazine | The Economist">{{Cite news|url=https://www.1843magazine.com/content/features/giles-whittell/andre-geim|title=The godfather of graphene|date=12 August 2014|newspaper=The Economist|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref> She visited the [[University of Oxford]], [[University of Cambridge]] and [[Imperial College London]] to deliver seminars on her PhD research.<ref name="Cover Story - The godfather of graphene | 1843 magazine | The Economist" /> Eventually, she joined the [[University of Bristol]] as a postdoctoral researcher.<ref name=":1" /> 
She moved to [[Nijmegen]] where she worked as a laboratory assistant.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HYpZDwAAQBAJ&q=irina+grigorieva+manchester&pg=PT48|title=The Graphene Revolution: The weird science of the ultra-thin|last=Clegg|first=Brian|date=5 July 2018|publisher=Icon Books|isbn=978-1-78578-377-7|language=en}}</ref> 

Grigorieva suggested to Geim that he use a frog to demonstrate [[magnetic levitation]], for which [[Geim]] won the [[Ig Nobel Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.sciencemuseum.org.uk/secret-of-scientific-creativity-revealed-by-andre-geim-godfather-of-graphene/|title=Secret of Scientific Creativity revealed by Andre Geim|last=says|first=Clive Richardson|website=Science Museum Blog|date=28 May 2015 |language=en-GB|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref>

She joined the [[University of Manchester]] in 2001, where she works in the Condensed Matter Physics group.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.condmat.physics.manchester.ac.uk/people/academic/irinagrigorieva/|title=Irina Grigorieva (The University of Manchester)|website=www.condmat.physics.manchester.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref> When she joined the group, she started studying the adhesive mechanisms of the feet of [[gecko]] lizards.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.theengineer.co.uk/spiderman-comes-to-manchester/|title=Spiderman comes to Manchester|last=Administrator|first=System|date=2003-06-02|website=The Engineer|language=en-UK|access-date=2 July 2019|archive-date=2 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702205233/https://www.theengineer.co.uk/spiderman-comes-to-manchester/}}</ref> In 2003, she created a gecko-like adhesive that is self-cleaning and re-attachable.<ref name=":2" /> Grigorieva is a member of the Graphene Council.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thegraphenecouncil.org/blogpost/1501180/Graphene-Updates?tag=Irina+Grigorieva|title=Graphene Updates - The Graphene Council|website=thegraphenecouncil.org|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref> 

Grigorieva is a Professor of Physics at the [[University of Manchester]] and Director of the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] Centre for Doctoral Training in Science and the Applications of Graphene.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.manchester.ac.uk/discover/news/professor-irina-grigorieva-awarded-the-2019-david-tabor-medal-and-prize/|title=Professor Irina Grigorieva awarded the 2019 David Tabor medal and prize|website=Professor Irina Grigorieva awarded the 2019 David Tabor medal and prize|language=en|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref> She works on the electronic and magnetic properties of [[two-dimensional materials]]. She is interested in [[Superconductivity|superconducting]] materials and the application of [[graphene]] in [[spintronics]]. In 2013, she was the first to demonstrate that graphene could be magnetic through the use of [[non-magnetic]] atoms and vacancies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scitechdaily.com/graphene-turned-magnetic-by-university-of-manchester-researchers/|title=Graphene Turned Magnetic by University of Manchester Researchers|date=9 January 2012|website=SciTechDaily|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sepioni|first1=M.|last2=Nair|first2=R. In 2015, she demonstrated that it is possible to switch the magnetism in graphene on and off.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.scienceandindustrymuseum.org.uk/2d-material-age/|title=Dawn of the Age of 2D Materials|last=authors|first=Guest|date=15 September 2016|website=Science and Industry Museum 2019|archive-date=2 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702205234/https://www.materialstoday.com/carbon/news/graphene-balloons-dont-burst-under-pressure/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Grigorieva used [[graphene]] as a filter to remove [[Subatomic particle|subatomic particles]], including taking protons from [[heavy water]].<ref name="New use discovered for graphene | Laboratory News">{{Cite web|url=https://www.labnews.co.uk/news/new-use-discovered-graphene-13-01-2016/|title=New use discovered for graphene|last=Admin|date=13 January 2016|website=Laboratory News|language=en-US|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref> This includes removing [[deuterium]] for the cleaning of [[Nuclear Waste|nuclear waste]].<ref name="New use discovered for graphene | Laboratory News" />

=== Awards and honours ===
* 2019 [[Institute of Physics]] [[David Tabor Medal and Prize]]<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/subject/tabor/tabor-medallists/page_38603.html|title=David Tabor medal recipients|website=iop.org|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref>

=== Personal life ===
Grigorieva and husband, physicist Sir [[Andre Geim]], have a daughter.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/sir-andre-geim-interview-father-of-graphene-i-m-an-alien-among-my-own-and-on-my-own-among-aliens-9850167.html|title='I'm an alien among my own, and on my own among aliens' says 'father of graphene'|date=9 November 2014|website=The Independent|language=en|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref> She serves on the Board of Governors of [[Withington Girls' School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wgs.org/about-withington/governors/|title=Governors|website=Withington Girls' School|access-date=2 July 2019|archive-date=25 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160825072529/http://www.wgs.org/about-withington/governors/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
